retail-business-owners-cost-cuts-that-hu.headline: Retail Business Owners - Cost Cuts That Hurt Profitability
retail-business-owners-cost-cuts-that-hu.author: Steve Thompson
retail-business-owners-cost-cuts-that-hu.core: Posted in last 7 days Retail Business Owners - Cost Cuts That Hurt Profitability Cutting Costs Doesn’t Always Improve Your Bottom Line. Sometimes It Can Hurt It. One of my biggest takeaways from my recent conversation with Mark Cardone, Retail Real Estate on The Bottom Line_powered by Integrity Cost Consulting was that business owners need to think carefully about the difference between reducing expenses and improving profitability. Mark, founder of Rooftop Realty, joined me for a return appearance to share his perspective on commercial real estate, business growth, and the decisions that can make or break a business. A few things from our conversation really stuck with me. The cheapest location isn’t necessarily the most profitable. Mark discussed the importance of customer demographics, convenience, and neighboring businesses. Paying more for the right location can generate substantially more revenue than choosing a less expensive alternative. Not all cost reductions are good decisions. Mark shared how shopping malls eliminated amenities to reduce operating expenses, only to potentially diminish the customer experience that attracted visitors in the first place. Your lease deserves more attention than you might think. Annual rent increases, maintenance responsibilities, and building operating expenses can quietly erode profitability when business owners don’t fully understand or regularly review their agreements. Your neighboring businesses may be an untapped opportunity. Sometimes the best growth strategy isn’t spending more on marketing. It’s finding ways to collaborate with businesses that already attract the customers you want to reach. That second point particularly resonated with me. At Integrity Cost Consulting, we spend a lot of time helping businesses identify unnecessary expenses and improve profitability. However, I’ve always believed the objective shouldn’t be to spend less. It should be to spend smarter. There’s a big difference between eliminating waste and eliminating value. A business can negotiate a lower rent, reduce services, or cut operating expenses and still end up in a worse financial position if those decisions negatively impact revenue or the customer experience. My biggest takeaway? Don’t evaluate expenses in isolation. Understand the value they create and how they contribute to your overall profitability. Mark brought some great real-world examples, practical advice, and plenty of personality to our conversation. And one more thing… Who am I missing? One of the things I enjoy most about hosting The Bottom Line is learning from business leaders with different experiences, perspectives, and stories worth sharing. I’m always looking to connect with interesting CFOs, CEOs, entrepreneurs, and business leaders across industries. Who would you like to hear from on a future episode? Tag them below, introduce us, or send me a message. I’d genuinely appreciate your suggestions! #TheBottomLine #BusinessGrowth #Profitability #Leadership #CommercialRealEstate

We’ve studied Netflix, Airbnb, Uber, and Facebook from every imaginable angle. Their journeys are extraordinary, and there’s plenty to learn from them. But I’m increasingly curious about another group: founders who built lesser-known companies, delivered strong returns to their investors, and led their businesses to successful exits without ever entering the startup hall of fame. What did their journey look like from the inside? The struggles that never made it into a pitch deck. The signals they almost missed. The moment they decided to keep building, change direction, or sell. And how they made that decision with incomplete information and years of their lives on the line. I suspect these stories hold lessons that many founders can see themselves in. There’s a wealth of experience here that deserves more airtime. I’d love to speak with exited founders in my network, hear their stories, and pick their brains. If that’s you or someone you think I should meet, let’s connect. young-adults-in-india-mid20s-porn-addict.author: Difficult_Excuse9971
young-adults-in-india-mid20s-porn-addict.core: Posted in last 7 days Young Adults in India Mid-20s - Porn Addiction Impact on Confidence Learning more about porn addiction and its effects, especially in young adults in India in their mid-20s. Hi, I'm a writer, and I'm currently looking to speak with people who have suffered from problematic pornographic use and how it affected their lives, their confidence, self-esteem, focus, etc. I'm doing this for an article and want to gather first-person accounts of this problem. No one's true identity will ever be mentioned unless you explicitly choose to. This issue is a taboo that's plaguing many of our generation, and it needs a nuanced rather than demonised discussion around it. Please feel free to DM me, or you can simply email me at [email redacted] Any contacts of foundations doing work in this area, especially in Pune or urban places in Maharashtra, would also be much appreciated.
